label: D2 after choosing a2, previous trial rewarded, early-to-mid episode (trials ~5-55)
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires only at D2 (never at D1 or GO), and almost only when the action just taken (in_action at D2) was a2 (99.9% of activation mass). Rate is further gated by the previous trial having been rewarded (prev_reward=1 carries 98.6% of mass) and by episode time: it is strongly active in trials ~10-50, weaker in 0-9, fades by 50-59 and is silent after trial 60, so it seems to track slow drift in the hidden state across the episode, not any input. Correlates: good=S2 and high value (the a2-rewarded regime). It does not fire after a1 choices, after unrewarded previous trials (mostly), or in late episodes. Reached state (S1 vs S2) and common/rare only mildly change the rate. Phase+a2 alone has recall 0.999 but precision 0.28; adding prev_reward and the episode-time window gives dev F1 0.83, mass recall 0.97. All variables are observed (ep_trial is not an input, but it is a past/internal quantity, not a future one).

issues: The label leaves out a systematic gate: the previous trial's transition. Inside the original predicate, the slice with prev_common==0 (previous trial rare and rewarded) has precision 0.009 and mass recall 0.0005 on dev, so the unit is essentially silent there. With prev_common==1, precision is 0.89. These rare-rewarded previous trials are the main source of the original predicate's false positives (precision 0.77 dev / 0.755 test).

The explanation says common vs rare 'change the rate only a little'. That holds for the current trial's transition (common 0: rate 0.054; common 1: 0.049). It is badly wrong for the previous trial's transition, which is the deciding variable once prev_reward==1. Unrewarded previous trials behave the same way: (D2 & a2 & prev_reward==0 & prev_common==1) has zero activations, and the small leftover prev_reward==0 activity (about 1% of the mass) comes from prev rare-unrewarded trials (precision 0.12).

In practice the unit fires at D2 after an a2 choice that follows a previous a2->S2 common, rewarded trial. prev_action==1 holds only 0.1% of the mass, and (D2 & a2 & prev_reward==1 & prev_state==1) has precision 0.002. Read with the residual prev rare-unrewarded activity, the pattern looks like 'staying on a2 after outcome evidence that S2 is good', not just 'previous trial rewarded'.

Checks that held up: no activity at D1 or GO (0 of 380k steps each). in_action==2 holds 99.9% of the mass. prev_reward==1 holds 98.6%. The episode-position pattern is as described: 0.067 for trials 0-9, about 0.11 for 10-29, 0.026 for 50-59, about 0 from 60 on. good==1 is strongly suppressive (precision 0.32 inside the predicate).
The original test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.755, R 0.907, F1 0.824, mass recall 0.973).

Tool oddity, not used as evidence: the profile's 'top activating windows' show core cells labelled a1 with activation 1.00. Scoring contradicts this (only 52 active steps with in_action==1, 0.1% of the mass), and the header reports magnitude mean/max as 0.000. The window rendering or magnitude display looks unreliable for this unit, so all conclusions above rest on the scores.
